title: 2008 AMC 8 Problem 11
statement: Each of the \(39\) students in the eighth grade at Lincoln Middle School has one dog or one cat or both a dog and a cat. Twenty students have a dog and \(26\) students have a cat. How many students have both a dog and a cat?

solutions.text:
The number of people that have both animals is equal to the number of people that own a cat plus the number of people that own a dog minus the number of people that own either.

Therefore, the number of people who own both is \[20+26-39 = 7.\]

Thus, the answer is A .
hints: Adding dog owners and cat owners counts students with both pets twice.
Use inclusion-exclusion with the total number of students as the union.
